Algebra I · Lesson 5.2

Substitution

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Two numbers satisfy y=3x+26y=3x+26 and x+y=2x+y=2. Run 5.1's search on the second equation, (0,2)(0,2), (1,1)(1,1), (2,0)(2,0), and every candidate fails the first. The pair hides among negatives, where listing never ends. The first equation is not one more claim to test. It says what yy is. At the solution, yy and 3x+263x+26 are the same number.

Problem
The first equation says yy equals 3x+263x+26, so write 3x+263x+26 in yy's place in x+y=2x+y=2. One equation in one variable remains. Solve it and enter xx.
Show a hint
  • The swap leaves an equation with only xx in it, exactly the kind chapter 4 solves.
  • After the substitution the claim reads x+(3x+26)=2x+(3x+26)=2. Collect the left side to 4x+26=24x+26=2.
Show the full solution
x+(3x+26)=2x+(3x+26)=2 collects to 4x+26=24x+26=2, so 4x=−244x=−24 and x=−6x=−6​. The first equation names yy, so its expression can stand wherever yy stands.
Problem
The partner is still missing. Substitute x=−6x=−6 into y=3x+26y=3x+26, the equation already solved for yy, and enter yy. Check the pair in both original equations first.
Show a hint
  • The solved-form equation computes yy from any xx, including this one.
  • Substituting gives y=3(−6)+26y=3(−6)+26. Keep the parentheses around the negative value.
Show the full solution
y=3(−6)+26=−18+26=8y=3(−6)+26=−18+26=8​. Check (−6,8)(−6,8) in both originals, 8=3(−6)+268=3(−6)+26 and −6+8=2−6+8=2, so the pair passes the full 5.1 test.
Key idea
Substitution. When one equation gives a variable as an expression, replace that variable in the other equation with the expression. One variable remains, chapter 4 solves it, and back-substituting into the solved-form equation finds the partner. The swap is legal because at the solution pair the variable and its expression are the same number, the evaluating idea from 2.2, so the rewritten equation makes exactly the claim the old one made, equivalent in 4.2's sense.
Problem
The system x=3y+22x=3y+22 and x+2y=112x+2y=112 leads with xx this time. Replace xx in the second equation with 3y+223y+22, solve for yy, back-substitute, and enter xx.
Show a hint
  • Either letter can be the pre-solved one. The steps do not change. Replace the letter that equals an expression.
  • (3y+22)+2y=112(3y+22)+2y=112 collects to 5y+22=1125y+22=112.
Show the full solution
(3y+22)+2y=112(3y+22)+2y=112 gives 5y+22=1125y+22=112, so 5y=905y=90, y=18y=18, and x=3(18)+22=76x=3(18)+22=76​. The ask is xx, so the back-substitution is not optional.

So far the replaced letter stood alone. In 4x+3y=474x+3y=47 the yy is tripled, and 3y3y means three copies of all of yy, so whatever stands in for yy must arrive as one unit. With y=2x+7y=2x+7, the incoming expression takes the seat as a block, not a piece at a time.

Key idea
Substitute in parentheses. Replacing the yy of 3y3y with 2x+72x+7 must produce 3(2x+7)3(2x+7), which distributes by 2.1 to 6x+216x+21. Written bare, 4x+3⋅2x+74x+3⋅2x+7 adds 77 where the faithful line adds 2121, so every line after it is about a different equation, and the pair it lands on fails the original check. A coefficient slot means parentheses, no exceptions.
Problem
Solve the system y=3x−16y=3x−16 and 5x+2y=785x+2y=78. The 2y2y doubles the whole expression, so substitute in parentheses, distribute, and enter x+yx+y.
Show a hint
  • Substitute the whole expression 3x−163x−16 for yy in the second equation, with parentheses around all of it.
  • 5x+2(3x−16)=785x+2(3x−16)=78 distributes to 11x−32=7811x−32=78.
Show the full solution
5x+2(3x−16)=785x+2(3x−16)=78 gives 11x−32=7811x−32=78, so 11x=11011x=110 and x=10x=10, then y=3(10)−16=14y=3(10)−16=14 and x+y=24x+y=24​.
Problem
A student substitutes y=2x−3y=2x−3 into x+4y=51x+4y=51 and writes x+4⋅2x−3=51x+4⋅2x−3=51, no parentheses. That line gives x=6x=6, then y=9y=9, and the check fails, since 6+4(9)=426+4(9)=42, not 5151. Redo the substitution with the parentheses it needed and enter the correct xx.
Show a hint
  • In 4y4y, the 44 must multiply everything yy is, not just the first piece.
  • The faithful line is x+4(2x−3)=51x+4(2x−3)=51. Distribute, then collect.
Show the full solution
x+4(2x−3)=51x+4(2x−3)=51 gives 9x−12=519x−12=51, so 9x=639x=63 and x=7x=7​, with y=2(7)−3=11y=2(7)−3=11 and 7+44=517+44=51. The bare line subtracted 33 where the equation subtracts 1212.

Nobody pre-solves equations for you outside a lesson. When neither equation arrives in solved form, pick a letter, solve for it with 4.3's moves, then substitute exactly as before. One isolate is the whole cost, and the rest of the run does not change.

Problem
Neither equation of 3x+y=323x+y=32 and 7x+2y=757x+2y=75 is solved for a letter, but the first is one 4.3 move away. Solve it for yy, substitute into the second, and enter yy. Check the pair in both originals.
Show a hint
  • Subtracting 3x3x from both sides pre-solves the first equation for yy.
  • Substitute y=32−3xy=32−3x into the second equation to get 7x+2(32−3x)=757x+2(32−3x)=75.
Show the full solution
y=32−3xy=32−3x, so 7x+2(32−3x)=757x+2(32−3x)=75 collects to x+64=75x+64=75 and x=11x=11, then y=32−33=−1y=32−33=−1​. Check, 33+(−1)=3233+(−1)=32 and 77−2=7577−2=75, both originals pass.
Key idea
Choose the coefficient-1 letter. A letter with coefficient 11 or −1−1 isolates without dividing, so the rest of the work has no fractions in it. Any choice is legal, and every choice gives the same solution pair. The only difference is the arithmetic, and cleaner arithmetic means fewer chances to slip, so scan both equations for a coefficient of 11 or −1−1 before isolating anything.
Problem
In 3x−y=203x−y=20 and 5x+2y=45x+2y=4 the yy has coefficient −1−1. Solving the first for yy still takes one move, y=3x−20y=3x−20. Substitute into the second equation and enter yy.
Show a hint
  • Coefficient −1−1 is as cheap as coefficient 11. No dividing happens on the way to solved form.
  • 5x+2(3x−20)=45x+2(3x−20)=4 collects to 11x−40=411x−40=4.
Show the full solution
5x+2(3x−20)=45x+2(3x−20)=4 gives 11x−40=411x−40=4, so 11x=4411x=44, x=4x=4, and y=3(4)−20=−8y=3(4)−20=−8​. Nothing stops a solution pair from being negative.
Problem
One letter in 4x+y=1984x+y=198 and 2x+3y=2042x+3y=204 isolates without fractions. Find it, isolate it, substitute, solve the system, and enter the product xyxy.
Show a hint
  • Only yy in the first equation has coefficient 11, so isolating it costs one 4.3 move and no fractions.
  • Substituting y=198−4xy=198−4x into the second equation gives 2x+3(198−4x)=2042x+3(198−4x)=204.
Show the full solution
Isolate y=198−4xy=198−4x, then 2x+3(198−4x)=2042x+3(198−4x)=204 gives 2x+594−12x=2042x+594−12x=204, so −10x=−390−10x=−390 and x=39x=39, then y=198−156=42y=198−156=42. The product is 39⋅42=163839⋅42=1638​. Check, 2(39)+3(42)=78+126=2042(39)+3(42)=78+126=204.
Fun fact
Babylonian clay tablets from around 1800 BCE pose problems giving the sum and the difference of two unknown quantities, then solve them by a fixed rule, half the sum shifted either way by half the difference, in words with no symbols at all.
Problem
Solve the system y=2x+4y=2x+4 and 6x+2y=336x+2y=33. Nothing requires the pair to be whole. Check the pair in both equations, then enter xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The run is the usual one. Only the ending is not a whole number.
  • 6x+2(2x+4)=336x+2(2x+4)=33 collects to 10x+8=3310x+8=33.
Show the full solution
6x+2(2x+4)=336x+2(2x+4)=33 gives 10x+8=3310x+8=33, so 10x=2510x=25 and x=2510=52x=1025​=25​​, with y=2⋅52+4=9y=2⋅25​+4=9. Check, 9=5+49=5+4 and 15+18=3315+18=33, both originals pass.

Sometimes the substitution erases the letter entirely. Every xx-term cancels, and a statement with no variable in it is left behind, true or false on its own. 4.3 met this inside one equation. Here the leftover statement is a verdict about the whole system, and the next two problems read one of each kind.

Problem
Substitute y=4x+5y=4x+5 into 8x−2y=68x−2y=6 and simplify. Every xx-term cancels and a number statement is left. Decide what it means and enter the number of solutions of the system.
Show a hint
  • 4.3 met a vanishing variable inside one equation. The number statement left behind is the verdict.
  • 8x−2(4x+5)8x−2(4x+5) simplifies to −10−10, and the equation claims that equals 66.
Show the full solution
8x−2(4x+5)=8x−8x−10=−108x−2(4x+5)=8x−8x−10=−10, so the substituted equation reads −10=6−10=6, false at every xx, and the system has 00​ solutions. No pair can make both claims true at once.
Key idea
When the letter disappears. A false statement means the two claims conflict at every pair, so the system has no solution. That is 5.1's m+n=67m+n=67 and m+n=73m+n=73 situation, reached by algebra instead of by staring. A true statement means the second equation repeats the first, so every pair solving one solves both, and the solutions are infinitely many. Substitution is not failing in either case. It is reporting the count.
Problem
Substituting y=2x+6y=2x+6 into 4x−2y=−124x−2y=−12 leaves −12=−12−12=−12, true for every xx. Infinitely many pairs solve the system, but not every pair does. Of (2,10)(2,10), (6,18)(6,18), (10,26)(10,26), (8,20)(8,20), enter how many solve the system.
Show a hint
  • Every pair solving the first equation solves both. Pairs off it solve neither.
  • Test each pair in y=2x+6y=2x+6, first value in for xx, second in for yy.
Show the full solution
10=4+610=4+6, 18=12+618=12+6, and 26=20+626=20+6 pass, but 2(8)+6=22≠202(8)+6=22=20, so 33​ of the four solve the system. Infinitely many means every pair satisfying the equation, and only those.
Problem
Two numbers satisfy x−2y=45x−2y=45 and 2x+3y=3982x+3y=398. Isolate the coefficient-1 letter, substitute, solve the system, check the pair in both equations, and enter the product xyxy.
Show a hint
  • Only xx carries coefficient 11. One 4.3 move gives x=2y+45x=2y+45.
  • Substituting gives 2(2y+45)+3y=3982(2y+45)+3y=398, which collects to 7y+90=3987y+90=398.
Show the full solution
Isolate x=2y+45x=2y+45, then 2(2y+45)+3y=3982(2y+45)+3y=398 gives 7y+90=3987y+90=398, so 7y=3087y=308 and y=44y=44, then x=2(44)+45=133x=2(44)+45=133. Check, 133−88=45133−88=45 and 266+132=398266+132=398. The product is 133⋅44=5852133⋅44=5852​.

All the systems in this lesson had a letter with coefficient 11 or −1−1, or were already solved for a letter. There is no letter to isolate cleanly in 9x+7y=769x+7y=76 and 5x+8y=725x+8y=72, so any isolation starts with a division and brings fractions into every later step. Lesson 5.3 introduces elimination, a second method for exactly this case.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The numbers xx and yy satisfy y=x+25y=x+25 and x+y=71x+y=71. Substitute the expression for yy into the second equation, solve, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Substituting gives x+(x+25)=71x+(x+25)=71, so 2x+25=712x+25=71, 2x=462x=46, and x=23x=23​. Then y=48y=48, and 23+48=7123+48=71 checks.
Practice
The system y=2xy=2x and 3x+y=403x+y=40. The expression for yy has no constant term, and the steps are exactly the same. Substitute, solve, back-substitute, and enter yy.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 3x+2x=403x+2x=40, so 5x=405x=40 and x=8x=8. Back-substituting, y=2(8)=16y=2(8)=16​. The pair checks in the second equation, since 24+16=4024+16=40.
Practice
The system x=y+10x=y+10 and x+4y=30x+4y=30 leads with xx. Replace the xx of the second equation with y+10y+10, solve for yy, back-substitute, and enter xx.
Show the solution
(y+10)+4y=30(y+10)+4y=30 collects to 5y+10=305y+10=30, so 5y=205y=20 and y=4y=4. Then x=4+10=14x=4+10=14​. Check, 14+4(4)=3014+4(4)=30.
Practice
Solve the system y=2x+34y=2x+34 and 2x+y=1502x+y=150. Substitute, solve for xx, then finish with a back-substitution and enter yy.
Show the solution
2x+(2x+34)=1502x+(2x+34)=150 gives 4x=1164x=116, so x=29x=29, and y=2(29)+34=92y=2(29)+34=92​. Check, 58+92=15058+92=150.
Practice
In y=x−5y=x−5 and 3x+2y=503x+2y=50, the yy slot carries a coefficient, so the substitution needs parentheses. Substitute, distribute, solve the system, and enter x+yx+y.
Show the solution
3x+2(x−5)=503x+2(x−5)=50 distributes to 3x+2x−10=503x+2x−10=50, so 5x=605x=60 and x=12x=12. Then y=12−5=7y=12−5=7 and x+y=19x+y=19​. Check, 3(12)+2(7)=36+14=503(12)+2(7)=36+14=50. Dropping the parentheses would give 3x+2x−5=503x+2x−5=50, which subtracts 55 where the equation subtracts 1010.
Practice
Solve the system y=2x+1y=2x+1 and 5x+3y=805x+3y=80. The 3y3y takes the whole expression as one unit. Substitute with parentheses, distribute, and enter yy.
Show the solution
5x+3(2x+1)=805x+3(2x+1)=80 distributes to 5x+6x+3=805x+6x+3=80, so 11x=7711x=77 and x=7x=7. Then y=2(7)+1=15y=2(7)+1=15​, and 35+45=8035+45=80 checks.
Practice
Substituting y=3x−7y=3x−7 into 2x+5y=612x+5y=61, a student writes 2x+5⋅3x−72x+5⋅3x−7, no parentheses. At every value of xx, the student's expression exceeds the faithful 2x+5(3x−7)2x+5(3x−7) by the same fixed amount. Enter that amount.
Show the solution
The faithful expression is 2x+15x−35=17x−352x+15x−35=17x−35 and the bare one is 2x+15x−7=17x−72x+15x−7=17x−7, a gap of 35−7=2835−7=28​ at every xx. The missing parentheses shrink the subtraction from 3535 to 77.
Practice
Neither equation of 4x+y=2314x+y=231 and 2x+3y=2332x+3y=233 is pre-solved. Isolate the coefficient-1 letter with one 4.3 move, substitute into the other equation, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Isolate y=231−4xy=231−4x, then 2x+3(231−4x)=2332x+3(231−4x)=233 gives 2x+693−12x=2332x+693−12x=233, so −10x=−460−10x=−460 and x=46x=46​. Then y=231−184=47y=231−184=47, and 92+141=23392+141=233 checks.
Practice
For x+5y=14x+5y=14 and 3x+4y=643x+4y=64, the letter that isolates cleanly is xx. Isolate it, substitute into the second equation, solve, and enter yy.
Show the solution
x=14−5yx=14−5y, so 3(14−5y)+4y=643(14−5y)+4y=64 gives 42−15y+4y=6442−15y+4y=64, then 42−11y=6442−11y=64, −11y=22−11y=22, and y=−2y=−2​, with x=14+10=24x=14+10=24. Check, 24−10=1424−10=14 and 72−8=6472−8=64.
Practice
Solve x=2y+3x=2y+3 and 3x+2y=113x+2y=11. The system leads with xx, and the answer is not a whole number. Enter yy as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
3(2y+3)+2y=113(2y+3)+2y=11 gives 6y+9+2y=116y+9+2y=11, so 8y=28y=2 and y=28=14y=82​=41​​, with x=2⋅14+3=72x=2⋅41​+3=27​. Check, 3⋅72+12=113⋅27​+21​=11.
Practice
In 4x+y=2484x+y=248 and 2x+3y=2542x+3y=254, one letter isolates without fractions and one does not. Pick well, solve the system, and enter the product xyxy.
Show the solution
Isolate y=248−4xy=248−4x, then 2x+3(248−4x)=2542x+3(248−4x)=254 gives 2x+744−12x=2542x+744−12x=254, so −10x=−490−10x=−490 and x=49x=49, then y=248−196=52y=248−196=52. The product is 49⋅52=254849⋅52=2548​. Check, 98+156=25498+156=254.
Practice
Substitute y=5x−3y=5x−3 into 10x−2y=1210x−2y=12 and simplify. The letter vanishes, and the left side sits the same fixed amount below 1212 at every xx. Enter that amount.
Show the solution
10x−2(5x−3)=10x−10x+6=610x−2(5x−3)=10x−10x+6=6, so the substituted equation reads 6=126=12, and the left side sits 12−6=612−6=6​ below the right side at every xx. The statement is false everywhere, so the system has no solution.
Practice
Substituting y=4x+1y=4x+1 into 12x−3y=−312x−3y=−3 leaves −3=−3−3=−3, a true statement. Every pair solving the first equation solves the system. Of the pairs (3,13)(3,13), (0,1)(0,1), (2,8)(2,8), (5,20)(5,20), enter how many solve it.
Show the solution
Testing each pair in y=4x+1y=4x+1, 13=12+113=12+1 and 1=0+11=0+1 pass, while 4(2)+1=9≠84(2)+1=9=8 and 4(5)+1=21≠204(5)+1=21=20 fail. So 22​ of the four solve the system.
Practice
For x−2y=1x−2y=1 and 6x+5y=746x+5y=74, isolate xx, substitute into the second equation, solve the system, and enter x+yx+y.
Show the solution
x=2y+1x=2y+1, so 6(2y+1)+5y=746(2y+1)+5y=74 gives 12y+6+5y=7412y+6+5y=74, then 17y=6817y=68 and y=4y=4, with x=2(4)+1=9x=2(4)+1=9. So x+y=13x+y=13​. Check, 9−8=19−8=1 and 54+20=7454+20=74.
Practice
One number is 5 less than double another, and the two add to 43. In symbols, y=2x−5y=2x−5 and x+y=43x+y=43. Solve the system and enter the larger number.
Show the solution
x+(2x−5)=43x+(2x−5)=43 gives 3x−5=433x−5=43, so 3x=483x=48 and x=16x=16, then y=2(16)−5=27y=2(16)−5=27. The larger number is 2727​. The problem asks for the larger of the two numbers, not for xx, so find both values before answering.
Practice
For 6x+y=376x+y=37 and 4x+3y=904x+3y=90, isolate the coefficient-1 letter, substitute, and enter xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
y=37−6xy=37−6x, so 4x+3(37−6x)=904x+3(37−6x)=90 gives 4x+111−18x=904x+111−18x=90, then 111−14x=90111−14x=90, 14x=2114x=21, and x=2114=32x=1421​=23​​, with y=37−9=28y=37−9=28. The clean isolate keeps fractions out of the middle of the work, not out of the answer.
Practice
In 3x−y=1063x−y=106 and 2x+2y=2202x+2y=220, the yy has coefficient −1−1, and 4.3's moves still isolate it, y=3x−106y=3x−106. Substitute, solve the system, and enter the product xyxy.
Show the solution
Substitute y=3x−106y=3x−106, so 2x+2(3x−106)=2202x+2(3x−106)=220 gives 8x−212=2208x−212=220, then 8x=4328x=432 and x=54x=54, with y=3(54)−106=56y=3(54)−106=56. The product is 54⋅56=302454⋅56=3024​. Check, 108+112=220108+112=220.
